description: Provider-neutral migration ledger for the immutable portable tenant baseline set. Declares the canonical apply order, the SHA-256 of every artifact, the apply principal and the control-plane role-bootstrap dependency.

ledger_store.note: The table in the tenant database is the source of truth for what a given database actually received. This manifest is the source of truth for what it should have received. Any disagreement is drift.

apply_principal.note: The runner connects as the non-superuser app_migration login and applies every step under SET ROLE app_owner, so app_migration owns no object.

reapply_semantics.note: A step already recorded with a matching SHA-256 is skipped and the run exits successfully. The baseline SQL is not internally idempotent, so re-executing it would fail; the runner must skip rather than re-run. Any disagreement between manifest, artifact file and ledger row is a hard failure instead.

down_migrations.note: The operations contract keeps reversal as an explicit break-glass action outside this ledger. No down step is declared, generated or accepted.

role_bootstrap.note: Roles are cluster-level objects and are not carried by pg_dump. A restore target must be prepared with this bootstrap before the dump is restored; the harness never uses pg_dumpall --roles-only, which would move credentials between clusters.

role_bootstrap_extensions.note: Additive control-plane prerequisite, deliberately NOT an edit to 000_control_plane_role_bootstrap.sql. app_ledger.role_bootstrap is a single-row append-only record of that artifact's digest, so changing its bytes would permanently break the ledger of every database already prepared with it. Step 004 checks for the role itself and refuses to apply without it; the digest is pinned here and asserted by postgres/tests/portable_migration_ledger_static_assertions.mjs.

Additive control-plane prerequisite of the AI execution path. Creates NO role: app_system belongs to the seven-role contract and already exists in every prepared cluster. The artifact changes exactly one attribute - ALTER ROLE app_system LOGIN - so the AI layer connects as the principal the guard was designed around. Separate file for the same append-only-digest reason as the identity store extension. Step 007 applies either way (its grants and policies need no login); the login is what lets the AI path CONNECT, which is why this extension is declared against step 7 rather than carried inside it - roles are cluster objects a dump does not carry. The credential is assigned out of band, as for app_migration and app_runtime.

Additive control-plane prerequisite, deliberately NOT an edit to 000_control_plane_role_bootstrap.sql. app_machine is a seven-role contract member and already exists in every prepared cluster; this artifact changes exactly one attribute, LOGIN, so the ingest endpoint can connect as the principal step 009's policies were written for. A role is a cluster-level object that pg_dump does not carry and that app_migration, being NOCREATEROLE, cannot alter, so the attribute cannot live in the step itself. Step 009 applies correctly without it and simply has no principal to enter what it opens until the control plane has run this.

ledger_bootstrap.note: Creates the app_ledger store itself, so it cannot be recorded as a step in that store.

restore_procedure.dump: pg_dump --format=custom --role=app_owner, run as the non-superuser app_migration login
restore_procedure.restore: pg_restore --exit-on-error --role=app_owner into a target prepared with the role bootstrap; pg_dumpall --roles-only is never used
restore_procedure.note: A restore target needs a temporary, explicitly closed window so the AI SQL guard can be handed back to app_ai_runner and re-grant its own ACL. Without it pg_restore silently leaves the guard executable by PUBLIC and without its app_system grant, because a failed GRANT is a warning rather than an error.

steps.description: Portable business tables, identities, constraints, indexes and the seven final views.
Canonical users, provider identity mapping, transaction-local actor context, grants and RLS.
Portable stored functions, business triggers and the SELECT-only AI SQL guard.
Identity admin write path, actor resolver, roster read and the identity provider store schema. Carries the four changes attached to gate G3 as condition C3.

The atomic cross-store invite: one SECURITY DEFINER function writing the canonical rows and the identity-store account in a single transaction, plus the two INSERT grants it needs. Closes the known limit step 004 recorded. No new role and no new credential.

One btree index on public.messages (direction, sent_at DESC, id DESC), which turns the message keyset seek from a filter over a sequential scan into an index condition. Closes the known limit S13 parts 2 and 3 both carried. Plain CREATE INDEX rather than CONCURRENTLY, because the runner applies each step in one transaction and an interrupted concurrent build would leave an INVALID index the append-only ledger cannot express. Additive: no role, grant, function or credential.

The system write path: SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE on the five relations the server-owned jobs own (briefing_jobs, briefings, messages, leads, saved_searches), sequence usage for the two identity sequences among them, and one FOR ALL policy per relation gated on the published system actor - the nil uuid, well-formed but unassignable, because step 005 is the only user creator and accepts no caller-supplied id. Grants app_system its first table privileges; gives no DELETE, touches no other role, leaves the AI SQL guard SELECT-only. Written under the owner's role-only decision: applied only by explicit owner approval, never automatically.

One EXECUTE grant on public.pipeline_auto_advance() to app_system, and nothing else. The scheduled half of the reply classifier has no human actor and runs as the system principal, which step 007 gave DML on messages and leads but no way to run the fixed auto-advance procedure step 003 granted to app_runtime alone; it therefore labelled replies and stopped one step short of triage. The function is SECURITY DEFINER owned by app_owner with a pinned search_path, so the grant is the whole capability - the caller gains no privilege on leads or pipeline_events, and no table grant appears here. Opens no relation, no sequence, no policy and no other function; adds no DELETE; needs no control-plane prerequisite, because app_system is a seven-role contract member that already carries LOGIN. The AI SQL guard is untouched and stays SELECT-only: this function has side effects and is called as a named operation on a direct connection, never as guard SQL. Written under the same owner decision as step 007: applied only by explicit owner approval, never automatically.

The machine ingest path: public.agent_credential (one row per machine that may ingest, storing a SHA-256 of a 256-bit secret and never the secret), public.agent_ingest_batch (one row per credential and idempotency key, written in the same transaction as the rows it describes, with no status column because a failed batch rolls back and leaves no trace), and the write surface of app_machine - the seven-role contract's ingest principal, which until now held no grant of any kind. It gains SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on the seven relations the agent writes plus the two created here, no DELETE anywhere, and a column-level UPDATE on last_used_at alone of the credential table. Each FOR ALL policy is gated on public.machine_actor_instance(), which resolves the published actor to a live credential's instance and returns NULL for an absent, malformed, unknown, revoked or expired one - so revocation is enforced by the database on every statement, and a credential cannot write another notebook's rows. Section E adds the actorless resolver (the machine equivalent of identity_resolve_actor, refusing a foreign tenant before an actor is published) and three admin functions gated on public.is_app_admin() and granted to app_runtime alone, so no role holds raw DML on the credential table. Creates no role and changes no role attribute; the LOGIN a production deployment needs arrives through the pinned control-plane extension 000_machine_ingest_role_bootstrap.sql. Leaves the AI SQL guard SELECT-only and touches no other role's grants or policies. Written under the same owner decision as steps 007 and 008: applied only by explicit owner approval, never automatically.

One grant: USAGE on schema public to app_machine, and nothing else. Step 009 gave the machine principal tables, sequences, functions and policies but not the right to reach the schema they live in, so every one of them raised 42501 before any of its own privileges were consulted; app_machine was the first role to arrive at that boundary with no prior grants, which is why the omission was invisible beside app_runtime's in step 002 and app_system's in step 003. Found by the live suite on its first run against a real app_machine login. It is a new step rather than an edit to 009 because the ledger is append-only, 009 is applied and its digest is recorded: a correction to an applied step is a step. Grants no object privilege, adds no policy, creates nothing, touches no other role, and deliberately omits CREATE, so the machine principal still cannot add an object to public. Written under the same owner decision as steps 007 through 009: applied only by explicit owner approval, never automatically.
